For any $a$, $b > 0$, we have
\begin{align*}
f(a,a) &= a, \\
f(b,a+b) &= f(a+b,a+b) - f(a,a) = f(a+b,a+b) - a.
\end{align*}Adding $a$ to both sides, we get \[f(a,a+b) = f(a+b,a+b) - a + a = f(a+b,a+b).\]Letting $b=1$ (but since we have to remember that we're working in terms of natural numbers here, it's better to use $1 \times x$ than $x$, so let $\ell$ be the smallest possible factor of $x$ and pick $\ell$), we then get $f(x,\ell x) = f(\ell x, \ell x).$ This suggests that
\[f(x,\ell x) = \frac{x}{\ell} f(x,x).\]Setting $x = \ell x$, we obtain \[f(\ell x, \ell x) = \ell f(\ell x, \ell)\]hence, combining the last two formulas, we obtain \[f(x,\ell x) = \ell \cdot \frac{x}{\ell} f(x,x) = xf(x,x).\]So, $f(x,\ell x) = xf(x,x)$. Since $f(x,x) = x$, this means that $f(x,\ell x) = xf(x,x) = xf(x,x) = xf(x,x) = xf(x,x) = xf(x,x) = xf(x,x) = xf(x,x) = xf(x,x).$ Plugging in $x = 1$ and $y = 52$, we get $f(1,52) = 1 \cdot f(1,52) = f(1,52) = 1 \cdot f(1,52) = f(1,52) = 1 \cdot f(1,52) = f(1,52) = 1 \cdot f(1,52) = f(1,52) = 1 \cdot f(1,52) = f(1,52) = 1 \cdot f(1,52) = f(1,52).$

Thus, $f(1,52) = \boxed{52}$. The answer is 52
